exposure: Type of placenta previa (low-lying, marginal, partial, complete)
Coexistence of placenta previa with placenta accreta
cohort: 213 singleton pregnancies diagnosed with placenta previa using antenatal ultrasonography at a tertiary reference hospital between January 2014 and December 2015.
finding: The coexistence of placenta previa-accreta significantly increases maternal and neonatal morbidity, while complete placenta previa is associated with increased risks compared to low-lying, marginal, and partial types.
mod_finding: The previa-accreta group had a significantly higher number of previous caesarean sections, and complete placenta previa and previa-accreta groups showed significantly higher rates of hysterectomy.
birth_weight: The groups were similar with respect to birthweight.
gest_age: The groups were similar with respect to mean gestational week at birth.
